provenance: Constructed teaching examples, not experimental measurements or instrument specifications.
coordinate_convention: x is the dimensionless numerical m/z coordinate, x = M/(u*abs(z)); u denotes one dalton as a physical mass. Frequencies are in Hz unless the field name states kHz.
model_boundaries: TOF assumes negligible initial kinetic energy, fixed acceleration potential magnitude and field-free path length, nonrelativistic motion, no collisions, and corrected flight time tau = t - t0.
Equal acceleration voltage means equal energy per charge. The example does not assume equal total kinetic energy for different charge states.
Orbitrap f = C/sqrt(x) applies to the ideal axial field; chosen C is illustrative.
Ideal ICR f_c = e B/(2 pi u x) applies to unperturbed free cyclotron motion in uniform B. Actual trapped-ion detected frequency is generally shifted, including reduced cyclotron motion.
Orbitrap and ICR examples use separate chosen constants; their identical 100 kHz reference value is not a comparison of actual instrument performance.
DFT duration convention is N/fs. The time of the last sample relative to the first is (N-1)/fs; this endpoint detail does not change the stated DFT grid relation.
Fourier grid spacing is not FWHM, a measurement uncertainty, or a guaranteed resolvable frequency separation.
Zero padding changes DFT length without changing the recorded sample count or physical observation duration.
Existing resolution, ppm-error, and matching-window examples are retained; existing science checks must still pass.
